reports.title: ZIM Reports Industry Leading Third Quarter 2026 Profitability, Driven

guidance.heading: Full-Year 2026 Guidance
section: In 2026, the Company expects to generate Adjusted EBITDA between $3.3 billion and $3.5 billion and Adjusted EBIT between $2.0 and $2.2 billion. Previously the Company expected to generate Adjusted EBITDA of between $2.7 billion and $3.0 billion and Adjusted EBIT of between $1.4 billion and $1.7 billion.

desk.headline: Revenue up 53% to $2.71bn, beat; EPS $6.88 vs $1.02; full-year EBITDA and EBIT outlook raised again
results: Revenue rose 53% to $2.71bn as the average rate per container (TEU) jumped 55% to $2,480 and volumes rose 4% to 962k TEU.
Net income was $830m ($6.88 a share) vs $123m; it includes a $155m after-tax impairment reversal, partly offset by $41m of deal-related costs. Adjusted net income was $717m.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $1.33bn (49% margin) and adjusted EBIT $993m (37% margin), up from 33% and 15%.
Free cash flow of $1.22bn cut net debt to $1.86bn from $2.77bn at end-June; net leverage fell to 0.8x and cash net of financial debt was $3.29bn.
Dividend of $2.01 a share (about $243m) is payable on 8 Dec to holders on record at 30 Nov.

guidance.summary: ZIM raised its 2026 targets: adjusted EBITDA to $3.3–3.5bn from $2.7–3.0bn and adjusted EBIT to $2.0–2.2bn from $1.4–1.7bn.

points: Rates held up through late summer, but management noted some softening in recent weeks as customers delayed US-bound cargo to after year-end; it expects a pickup in January before an earlier Chinese New Year.
Transpacific volume rose about 8% to 446k TEU and intra-Asia 12%; the focus is on higher-value cargo such as e-commerce, data-centre parts and pharma.
Fast (expedited) services are being extended to the US West Coast, with the new ZX3 service from China to Los Angeles starting in December.
ZIM's own ships are not yet back on the Suez/Red Sea route although most big lines are returning; it will decide based on security, calling Yemen still unstable.
The orderbook is 56 ships (418k TEU) through 2029 and vessel cost per TEU is down about 30% since Q3 2022; management took no questions on the Hapag-Lloyd deal, still targeted to close in Q1 2027.
